# MCP Tool Design: Why Your AI Agent Is Failing (And How to Fix It)

## MCP Best Practices (6 Part Series)

## The Reports of MCP's Death Have Been Greatly Exaggerated

Scroll through developer forums in early 2026, and you'll find a recurring theme: MCP is dead. The takes range from dismissive ("just a fad") to resigned ("we tried it, our agents kept failing"). And the frustrations behind them are real. Teams are building MCP servers with 50+ tools, watching their agents stumble through tool selection, and concluding that the protocol itself is broken.

It isn't. MCP isn't dead; it's being used poorly. And the evidence for how to use it well is now overwhelming. [...] Over the past year, teams at GitHub, Block, and dozens of smaller shops have converged on the same set of principles. GitHub Copilot cut its tool count from 40 to 13 and saw measurable benchmark improvements. Block rebuilt its Linear MCP server three times, going from 30+ tools to just 2. The pattern is consistent: fewer tools, better descriptions, outcome-oriented design. The problem isn't the protocol. It's tool design.

This article lays out the framework. We'll start with the mental model that makes everything else click, the Capability Square, then walk through the anatomy of a well-designed tool. Subsequent articles in this series cover the quantitative evidence, description quality, and the anti-patterns that cause most failures.

## What Is MCP? (The 30-Second Version) [...] Same API. Three completely different MCP servers. Three different sets of tools, with different names, different descriptions, and different response shapes, because the business analyst for each server shares a domain with their business users and knows how those users actually frame their requests.

Here's the key insight: when you ask an LLM to auto-wrap an API, it lacks this domain context. It can't know which 20% matters because it doesn't know who the user is. Auto-generated MCP servers produce generic tool sets that serve no one well. The business analyst's judgment — encoded in tool selection, naming, and descriptions — is what makes an MCP server effective, and that judgment exists only because the analyst understands the business, not just the API.

## Why you should avoid using MCP in Claude Code and what to use instead

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open-source standard that allows AI models to seamlessly connect with external data sources, tools, and software systems.

> MCP is a plug-and-play technology, like USB, but for AI.

Despite all the benefits that MCP brings to daily interactions with AI, this technology has 5 critical problems that make it less usable in real product design work.

In this article, I want to explain 5 reasons why using MCP is a bad idea and what you should use instead.

### Problem #1: MCP Adds Extra Level of Complexity

MCP is typically compared to API.

At that point, the problem is no longer “can the LLM call a tool?” The problem is whether the organization has designed a serious AI-facing interface to its business systems. That is what MCP is becoming.

The Model Context Protocol started in a developer-heavy world. Local servers, coding assistants, filesystem tools, GitHub tools, and IDE integrations made it easy to see MCP as a developer convenience. That history matters, but it is too small a frame for where MCP is going.

MCP is the integration contract between AI experiences and real-world systems. It is how an AI client gets governed access to data, actions, workflows, prompts, resources, tasks, and user interfaces. It is how a business turns a general LLM into something that can operate… [...] Member-only story

# 11 Mistakes about MCP That Hold Back Real AI Use Cases

A team starts with a simple goal: “Let our AI assistant answer questions about customer accounts.”  
The first demo works. Someone wires an MCP server to a CRM API. The assistant can search customers, read opportunities, and summarize recent tickets. The room is impressed.

Then the real use cases arrive. A sales manager asks for renewal risk by region. A finance analyst asks whether discounts violate policy. A customer success lead asks for open support cases, usage trends, and payment status in a single response. Legal asks who approved which action. Security asks why the server uses a shared API key. The business asks why two assistants define “active customer” differently.

results.content:
MCP is USB-C for AI.

It provides the model with 3 things

   Tools :the functions
   Resources :static documents
   Prompts :pre-defined instructions

Here’s how it works:

## The Old Way:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image 15

Source: Image by the author.

AI Tool #1 needs custom code to talk to Gmail  
AI Tool #1 needs DIFFERENT code to talk to Google Drive   
AI Tool #2 needs ANOTHER code to talk to Gmail  
AI Tool #2 needs YET ANOTHER code to talk to Google Drive
_Every tool had his own way of being setup which which was exhaustive and__time consuming_

30 different custom connections. Nightmare.

## The MCP Way:

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image 16

Source: Image by the author. [...] ## Real Examples from Early Adopters

From a designer:_“I used to spend 30 minutes gathering client feedback from emails, team notes, and project files. Now my AI does it in seconds. I actually have time to design now.”_

From a marketer:_“Campaign planning went from 3 hours to 20 minutes. Same quality. 90% less busywork.”_

From a developer:_“My AI can now see my codebase, documentation, and team discussions simultaneously. It’s like pair programming with someone who has photographic memory.”_

## The Bigger Picture

Here’s what’s really happening:

2020: We pressed buttons to control computers

2022: ChatGPT let us use words

2024: MCP let AI actually see our scattered work across different tools Anthropic

2025: This becomes the new normal [...] Image 16

Source: Image by the author.

Gmail learns one language: MCP  
Google Drive learns the same language: MCP  
All AI tools learn that language: MCP Eveyone can talk to everyone!
_MCP__standerdized the connection of tools so every ai tool can connect with a tool (like USB-C) without making their own custom implementations_

One language. Universal compatibility.

## The Brilliant Part

Here’s what makes MCP special:

Old way: YOU build custom connections between your AI and every app

MCP way: The APPS build their own MCP connection once

Now any MCP-compatible AI can connect instantly.

Think about what this means:

Gmail builds ONE MCP server.

Now every AI in the world can connect to it:

   ✅ ChatGPT? Works.
   ✅ Claude? Works.
   ✅ Your company’s custom AI? Works.
